newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. June retail sales up 0.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. June retail sales up 0.5 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Commerce Department reported June retail sales rose 0.5 percent compared to a downwardly revised 0.3-percent decline in May.
Economists in a Reuters survey had expected a 0.2-percent rise in sales, and a 0.5-percent increase minus the hefty automobile component.
TIM O'NEILL, CHIEF ECONOMIST, HARRIS BANK/BANK OF MONTREAL: "I would tend to put more emphasis on the ex-autos figure," which was weaker than had been expected.
O'Neill was speaking on Reuters Financial Television.
ASTRID ADOLFSON, FIRST VICE PRESIDENT AND AN ECONOMIST, MCM MONEYWATCH INC: "(The report) was a lot more mixed than I think most people had assumed.
"On the whole, you have to go with the revisions down the prior month, which are indicative that the consumer is just a little less anxious to spend than you would have assumed otherwise," he added.

KEVIN FLANAGAN, FIRST VICE PRESIDENT AND AN ECONOMIST, DEAN WITTER SECURITIES INC: "The June retail sales figure was a better indicator of how the consumer stands as the second quarter comes to a close.
"The weakness that you saw during April or May was due to inclement weather and record tax payments that had to be met," he added.

JOSEPH LIRO, CHIEF ECONOMIST, CIBC WOOD GUNDY SECURITIES CORP: "They're on the soft side. The surprise is the autos being up 1.1 percent and that's due to the different seasonals that the two different parts of the Commerce Department use when they adjust the autos.

"I think we're seeing a more sustained pick-up now in retail sales as we get through June and July. Part of the softness here was gas station sales and that's not volume but price. It's showing that the consumer is still very cautious at the end of the second quarter and doesn't change the expectation that we'll see a good bounce in the third quarter," he said.

LARRY WIPF, ECONOMIST, NORWEST CORP: "It just sort of confirms that we had the slowdown in the second quarter and that by the end of that quarter the econony was a little bit on the soft side, although the markets may eventually be jittery about whether the economy will be picking up in the third quarter, which I expect to be the case."
